overall_summary: Space anomalies and extreme cosmic environments drastically outperform abstract psychological concepts. Audiences respond strongly to highly visual, mind-bending physical paradoxes (e.g., burning ice, space oceans) over internal cognitive facts.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Cosmic Paradoxes & Sensory Space Facts
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet of Burning Ice' (1,053 views), 'The Largest Ocean in Space' (460 views), and 'What Does Outer Space Actually Smell Like?' (368 views) lead the channel's performance.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on extreme planetary conditions, cosmic anomalies, and sensory-based space facts using high-contrast visual hooks.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Sharks Are Older Than Trees?' (302 views) and 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' (183 views) perform significantly better than average.
winning_patterns.action: Create content comparing evolutionary timelines or bizarre biological traits using simple, shocking comparisons.

weak_patterns.evidence: Videos about fake memories (5 views), songs stuck in your head (17 views), and brain secrets (38 views) consistently fail to gain traction.
weak_patterns.action: Avoid abstract cognitive topics unless they can be framed with an immediate, shocking physical consequence or visual metaphor.
